findings.title: F-002 Citrix NetScaler Gateway 13.1-48.47: CVE-2023-4966
findings.description:
Outdated software with known vulnerabilities

Evidence: nmap NSE vulners: cpe:/a:citrix:netscaler_gateway:13.1: |     	CVE-2023-4966	9.4	https://vulners.com/cve/CVE-2023-4966	*EXPLOIT*
findings.mitigation:
Confirm the exact installed version and the vendor advisory for every CVE listed.
Apply the vendor fixed release (or the supported LTS branch) through the normal change process; emergency change if the CVE is in CISA KEV.
If patching must wait, apply the vendor workaround or put the service behind an allowlist / WAF virtual patch and document the compensating control with an expiry date.
Add the component to the software inventory (SBOM / CMDB) so the next advisory is matched automatically.
findings.impact: Citrix gateway supports 'Remote apps for engineering' (criticality 4/5, production, zone DMZ, internet-facing; data: internal). If exploited, an attacker could take control of the server and use it as a foothold for lateral movement or ransomware. CVE used by ransomware campaigns (KEV).

findings.title: F-009 Modbus/TCP exposed on 502/tcp
findings.description:
Industrial control protocol reachable from outside the OT zone

Evidence: nmap: 502/tcp open, service 'modbus Modbus TCP'
findings.mitigation:
Do NOT scan aggressively or patch live controllers: open a Management of Change (MOC) with Process Safety before any intervention.
Contain first: add a deny rule at the IT/OT boundary (conduit) so the protocol is only reachable from the engineering workstations and historian in the OT DMZ (zones and conduits model, IEC 62443 style).
Enable the controller's write-protection / run-mode key or protocol allowlist where the vendor supports it.
Plan the permanent fix (firmware, segmentation redesign) for the next scheduled turnaround and record it in the plant maintenance system.
findings.impact: PLC crude distillation unit supports 'Crude distillation unit control' (criticality 5/5, production, zone OT; data: internal). If exploited, an attacker could read or change process values or controller logic, with possible safety, environmental and production-loss consequences.
findings.references:
T0883
T0886
T1692
D3-NI
D3-ITF
D3-NTA

findings.title: F-018 Database/cache exposed on 1433/tcp
findings.description:
Database or cache service reachable without network restriction

Evidence: nmap: 1433/tcp open, service 'ms-sql-s Microsoft SQL Server 2016 13.00.5026'
findings.mitigation:
Bind the service to the application subnet only and add a host firewall rule allowing just the app servers.
Require authentication and TLS for every client connection; remove anonymous or default accounts.
Move the database into a dedicated data tier segment if it currently shares the user VLAN.

findings.title: F-022 VNC exposed on 5900/tcp
findings.description:
Remote administration service reachable from untrusted networks

Evidence: nmap: 5900/tcp open, service 'vnc VNC protocol 3.8'
findings.mitigation:
Remove the direct exposure: close the port on the perimeter firewall / security group for any source outside the admin allowlist.
Publish remote administration only through the corporate VPN or a zero-trust access broker with MFA.
Enforce Network Level Authentication (RDP) or key-only authentication (SSH) and disable password logins for privileged accounts.
Record the rule change with ticket ID in the firewall change log.

findings.title: F-024 SNMP exposed on 161/udp (unauthenticated read)
findings.description:
SNMP v1/v2c with default or guessable community string

Evidence: nmap: 161/udp open, service 'snmp SNMPv1 server; public' | snmp-info: enterprise: ciscoSystems
  engineIDFormat: unknown
  community: public (read)
findings.mitigation:
Migrate the device to SNMPv3 with authPriv (SHA-2 + AES).
If v2c must stay temporarily, set a long random read-only community and an ACL that allows only the NMS address.
Disable SNMP write access entirely.
findings.impact: Core switch supports 'Campus network' (criticality 5/5, production, zone IT; data: internal). If exploited, an attacker could reach internal systems directly from an untrusted network.

findings.title: F-030 FTP exposed on 21/tcp
findings.description:
Cleartext management or file-transfer protocol in use

Evidence: nmap: 21/tcp open, service 'ftp vsftpd 3.0.3'
findings.mitigation:
Replace Telnet with SSH and FTP with SFTP/FTPS; disable the cleartext daemon after migration.
Rotate every credential that was ever used over the cleartext protocol.
Block the cleartext port at the host firewall so it cannot be re-enabled silently.
findings.impact: Control room printer supports 'Shift reports printing' (criticality 1/5, production, zone IT; data: internal). If exploited, an attacker could take control of the server and use it as a foothold for lateral movement or ransomware.
